name: cascade-select
title: Cascade select
description: Pick a path through a hierarchy: columns that open to the right on desktop, a drill-down list on a phone and the full path in the field.
docs: options are { value, label, children?, disabled? } and the value is the path of values, one for each step (value, defaultValue, onValueChange). With changeOnSelect a choice that opens more can be the answer too, and a click picks it and opens it. On a screen wide enough for every level (14rem each) the panel shows one column per open level: Right opens a choice and moves into it, Left goes back, Up, Down, Home and End move in a column, Enter or Space picks, and Escape closes. Below that width the same panel is a drill-down list with a back row ("Back to Electronics") and the path above the list, and it opens at the level of the chosen choice. The field shows the whole path (separator sets what stands between the steps), with the front given up first when it is too long so the last step is read (when less than about three characters of the front would be left, it goes altogether, separator included, and the last step stands alone), and the full path as its tooltip. The search box flattens the tree to the paths that hold every word you type, ignoring case and accents, with the match in strong type; typing a letter on a choice sends it to the search, the first Escape empties it and Enter picks the first match. The columns are a tree, so every choice has aria-level, aria-setsize, aria-posinset and, when it opens more, aria-expanded and a spoken count of the choices inside it, and the depth you reach is announced; the matches of a search are a plain listbox. defaultOpen starts the panel open for a preview, and labels replaces every sentence. name sends the values of the path joined with a slash.
